items.briefing:
Cloudflare and Microsoft have jointly disrupted a major phishing operation called EvilTokens, which was using AI to bypass multi-factor authentication (MFA) — the extra login step many of us use to protect our accounts. This service was actively targeting Australians, meaning even people who had MFA enabled were at risk of having their accounts compromised. The takedown is good news, but similar services can re-emerge quickly.

Several security vendors including Palo Alto and Proofpoint have also released new AI-powered defences this week. **Practical tip:** MFA is still worth using, but if you receive an unexpected login prompt or verification request, don't approve it — contact your IT team first.

featured.title: Cloudflare & Microsoft disrupt EvilTokens phishing service
featured.summary: More than 12,000 inboxes were exposed as the kit used to bypass multi-factor authentication and sustain account access was taken offline.
